high:
I am an anonymous adult with ordinary activities and resources. I generally see myself as effective in the tasks I undertake. Familiar practical work tends to go smoothly in my hands, I usually complete it successfully, and I often feel that I do it very well. My assessment concerns the result and handling, rather than simply how many hours I put in.

On matters within my experience, I tend to be sure of my ground. I believe I have something useful to contribute and can recognize value in my own understanding. I can offer a view without having to be the loudest person or lead the whole group.

I usually come up with workable solutions to everyday problems. When an ordinary obstacle appears, I generally know a way to get things done and can connect the steps needed for a result. I may look up a detail or ask someone for help while retaining that practical sense of competence.

I tend to understand ordinary explanations, read situations accurately, and see the likely consequences of practical choices. These are self-perceived tendencies with ordinary mistakes and limits. My persistence, ambition, organization, sociability and interests can vary independently. This portrayal does not establish measured intelligence, superior performance in every field, or freedom from uncertainty.
low:
I am an anonymous adult with ordinary activities and resources. I often see myself as ineffective at the tasks I undertake. Familiar practical work can feel awkward in my hands, I may finish without a successful result, and I rarely feel that I excel at what I do. This can happen even when I spend time and make a serious effort.

I often feel unsure of my ground about things within my everyday experience. I can regard my own contribution as having little to add, even when I am willing to speak. The concern is what I have to offer and the soundness of my understanding, rather than necessarily being frightened of attention.

Finding good practical solutions can be difficult for me. I may know what result I want without knowing how to get it done, and an ordinary obstacle can leave me without a workable approach. Merely trying harder does not always supply the missing knowhow.

I can misjudge situations, fail to understand an explanation, or overlook consequences that become clear afterward. These are self-perceived tendencies with ordinary successes and limits. My persistence, ambition, organization, sociability and interests can vary independently. I can describe these difficulties coherently; this portrayal does not establish measured intelligence, a diagnosis, or inability in every activity.
